title: Each failing required job in a batch run wakes the batch runner as it fails
why: Owner chat 12:14 CST Nov 12, page item 559 pick c: "ah ok C is good go for it".
note: Each required job that fails posts the red-run notice as it fails, so the batch runner starts the drop and fix at once; the other jobs run on and name any second bad lane; the new head's run replaces the old one. R4's lint-first cancel stays beside it. Home: decision ci-wait-reads-run-status (the red-run comment rule). Why not cancel: red builds carry about 2 bad lanes each (147 drops over 74 builds, Nov 11 audit). Red first. Plan R53 (owner 13:07 CST Nov 12, restart-plan 4c91998): "i think any ci / merge relaterd thing should be just an alert for batch runner to either then address or bring to coordinator right". A CI or merge alarm (red main, a job at its time cap, a dropped check run) wakes the batch runner and opens no GitHub issue. This step is the one home for the main-run wake (coordinator 13:08 CST); PR #2745's cap alarm calls it. Triage sent R53 and the cap alarm lane's three questions to this lane 13:10 CST. Hand-in 13:11 CST Nov 12: draft PR #2860, head 33a8834c8; lane lint PASS only with --lint-unknown-ok (main's ci-job lacks this lane's failure() fix); round 1 FAIL fixed; kind normal. Covers the PR-comment wake only; the main-push wake is step main-push-wakes-runner. #2745 does not stack on #2860. Plan R55 (owner 13:19 and 13:21 CST Nov 12, restart-plan 4fefc9f, pick d: "Express lane, and cancel a running batch for it too"): a reviewed merge-flow lane goes to main as its own batch, ahead of all others; the batch runner cancels a batch run already in CI, and that batch then merges main in. Home: decision no-merge-during-batch-ci; skill ci-hygiene step 8 points to it (retrospective 13:23 CST, plan b152ca6). The owner chose this over the one-batch-in-turn rule.
